tossups.text: This figure is shown removing the weapons of another character in Jacques-Louis David's final painting. One painting contrasts the lines of this figure's body with the rolling hills in the background; that Giorgione work features this figure 'sleeping'. Flora offers this figure a cloak whilst Zephyrus blows on them forcefully from the top-left in another painting. This figure is shown reclining naked in a Titian painting named for Urbino. Shown arriving from the sea on a large scallop shell, for 10 points, name this figure whose 'birth' was depicted by Botticelli, the Roman goddess of love.

A Sanskrit group of these writings is found in the Panchatantra (PAHN-chah-THAN-trah). Marianne Moore translated a collection of these writings by Jean de la Fontaine. The Perry Index catalogs ones written by a Greek slave; those include stories about the "Tortoise and the Hare" and "Fox and the Grapes Out of Reach." For 10 points, name these stories that often contain animals and a moral lesson, many of which were written by Aesop.

This author wrote about his cross country trip in a camper named Rocinante with his poodle in Travels With Charley. In another work by this author Coyotito is shot and the titular object is thrown into the sea by Kino. In addition to The Pearl, this author wrote a novella about the migrant workers George and Lennie and another work in which the Joad family leaves Oklahoma. For 10 points, name this author of Of Mice and Men and The Grapes Of Wrath.

One section of this work opens with one character complaining to another because he did not join her for tennis, despite her bicycle pointing toward the oak as a sign. One recurrent image in this work, which was inspired by the marriage of the author's sister Anna to Hugo Philip, is that of a corpse carted out to a garden in a wheelbarrow. Late in this work, one character brings about the bankruptcy of a soda factory and the appointment of Allan to Norrland, as part of a scheme to have his daughter Judith marry the Colonel; earlier in this work, that same man collapsed after trying to dance to Halvorsen's "The Entrance of the Boyars", resulting in Kurt spending the night by his side. This work's second section ends with the Captain's death by stroke, though the first ends with a reprieve in the hateful marriage of Alice and Edgar before their silver anniversary. For 10 points, name this play in two parts by August Strindberg.

In the 1920s this man tried to extract gold from seawater, while earlier he was the first to demonstrate that oxidation and reduction take place at the electrodes. His study of the combustion of hydrocarbons led to the commercial "cracking" of natural oil into its components. Initially professor at Karlsruhe, he served from 1911-33 as director of the Kaiser-Wilhelm Institute for Physical Chemistry, but was forced out by the Nazis, despite having aided the WWI cause with his production of poison gas. For 10 points, who was this winner of the 1918 Nobel Prize for Chemistry for his method of ammonia production that was later modified by Bosch?

One version of this law states that heat cannot flow spontaneously from low temperature to high temperature. Another version of this law states that it is impossible to convert heat completely into work in a cyclic process. Maxwell proposed a thought experiment in which sorting air molecules seems to violate this law. For 10 points, identify this law, credited to French physicist Sadi Carnot, which states that "in a closed system, a process that occurs will tend to increase the total entropy of the universe."

One book from this country makes lists of "Vexatious things" and "Amusing things" and an author from this country wrote about the murder of a woodcutter from multiple perspectives. In addition to The Pillow Book and In A Grove, another work from this country told of a legendary seducer described as "shining" whose conquests include Lady Fujitsubo. For 10 points, name this country, home to Sei Shonagon and the author of The Tale of Genji, Lady Murasaki Shikibu.

In human anatomy, this structure is essential for metabolism regulation. It plays a key role in the endocrine system and is one of the most studied parts of human anatomy. For ten points, name this thyroid-related structure.
tossups.explanation: The thyroid is a key component of the Endocrine system, involved in metabolism regulation.

tossups.text: This literary character usurps the throne of King Pastoria, and is succeeded by Pastoria's daughter after she escapes from the witch Mombi. This character travels from Omaha in a hot air balloon, and is apprenticed to Glinda to learn real magic, although he uses stage magic tricks to confront the Scarecrow and Dorothy. For 10 points, name this magician who rules a fantasy land in a novel by L. Frank Baum.

In human physiology, this structure is essential for thymus gland. It plays a key role in the immune system and is one of the most studied parts of human anatomy. For ten points, name this lymph-related structure.
tossups.explanation: The lymph is a key component of the Immune system, involved in thymus gland.

tossups.text: This man's youngest son produced a prose translation of Paradise Lost and wrote religious poetry such as the Sacred Odes. The title character of one of this man's works commits suicide after being betrayed by his son Pharnace, while the title character of another of his works is the younger brother of Amurat whose death is ordered by a woman who loves him and who himself loves Atalide, an Ottoman princess. In his final tragedy, he wrote about the crowning of Joas after the titular usurper is overthrown. In addition to Mithridates, Bajazet, and Athalie [ah-thah-lee], he wrote plays about Britannicus and Esther. For 10 points, name this 17th-century French author best known for his tragedies Andromaque and Phèdre [fedd].

Nikolai Berdyaev and Paul Tillich were Christian thinkers from this school of thought. The author of A Happy Death denied belonging to this philosophical school, but is still associated with it. One person associated with an early form of this movement used pseudonyms such as Judge William, and described the dizziness of freedom in The Concept of Anxiety. The ideas of authenticity and existence preceding essence are important to this philosophical system. For 10 points, name this movement Jean-Paul Sartre ["SART"] described as "a humanism" in his Being and Nothingness.

One of this writer's stories follows Annemarie Johansen as she helps her friend Ellen escape from Nazi-occupied Denmark. A sequel to this author's most well-known book follows the weaver Kira, and that book ends with Jonah and Gabe fleeing the dystopian society they live in. For 10 points, identify this Newbery award winning author who wrote Number the Stars, Gathering Blue, and The Giver.

This technique's results are generally considered acceptable quality if rated twenty or higher on the Phred quality score. Characteristic squiggles are produced by samples passing through alpha-hemolysin connected to electrodes in a type of this technique developed by Oxford Nanopore. Bridge amplification is performed after adapters are ligated onto the ends of samples in this technique's library preparation step so they can adhere to a flow cell. Coverage and depth are considered when designing experiments with this technique, which has platforms designed by Illumina for its "next-generation" form. Target molecules incorporate fluorescent ddNTPs as "chain-terminators" in a type of this technique developed by Sanger. For 10 points, name this technique that determines the order of nucleotides in DNA.

Members of this group were brought to North America on the Woodhouse and Speedwell, and authored a petition to Peter Stuyvesant known as the Flushing Remonstrance. The Boston Martyrs, including Mary Dyer, were executed due to their membership in this group, though Roger Williams, a Puritan, allowed them to settle in Rhode Island. Another member of this group received a large tract of land as a debt repayment by King Charles II, where he founded a city with a name translating to "brotherly love." For 10 points, name this nonviolent Christian denomination whose members included George Fox and William Penn.

Moliere based part of his The Cheats of Scapin on this man's The Pedant Imitated. While studying under the mathematician Gassendi, he began to write fantastical stories of trips to the moon, and that extraterrestrial theme was continued in his Other Worlds, a satire based on Lucian's A True Story. In Other Worlds, he is escorted on the Moon by the Demon of Socrates. His poetic works included a harsh poem on Mazarin, but he is better know nas a fictional character who helps his rival Christian win the beautiful Roxanne. For 10 points, name this French playwright, satirist, and poet who is the title character of an Edmond Rostand play.

The Princess Anne militia failed to ambush this man's forces and were subsequently defeated at the Battle of Kemp's Landing. This man and Andrew Lewis forced Chief Cornstalk to sign the Treaty of Camp Charlotte, which relinquished his tribe's rights to hunting along the Ohio River. After this man ordered gunpowder to be transferred from Williamsburg to the Magdalen, he was forced to flee. A document written by this man was extended by Henry Clinton's Philipsburg Proclamation. This man created the "Ethiopian Regiment," which suffered a disastrous defeat at the Battle of Great Bridge. Following his loss at that battle, this man fled and allowed Robert Howe to raze Norfolk. This former governor of Virginia names a conflict between colonists and Mingo Native Americans that was ended at the Battle of Point Pleasant. For 10 points, name this British lord whose namesake "proclamation" allowed for freedom for any slave who fought for the British during the Revolutionary War.

A character in this novel remembers a remark made by his love interest about a woman conceiving out of wedlock after dreaming about a "siren" made of "sky and branches." The protagonist of this novel often quotes Shakespeare's Cymbeline, and wonders if her daughter Elizabeth is falling in love with Miss Kilman. In an attempt to follow the advice of Dr. Holmes, a character in this novel points out an airplane spelling out letters. The title character of this novel remembers kissing Sally Seton, and looks out the window during her party after learning about the suicide of Septimus Smith. For 10 points, Clarissa is the title housewife of what stream-of-consciousness Virginia Woolf novel?

This is the [emphasize] heavier of two elements found in tetrahedral units that can form sheets in phyllite ("FILL-ite") and chains in pyroxene ("pai-ROCK-seen"). This element names a class of rubber-like polymers used in sealants and flexible cookware. The rarity of chiral ("KAI-ruhl") compounds made of hydrogen and this element likely prevents it from acting as the basis of life, despite this third-period element's ability to have up to four covalent bonds. Packets of this element's namesake water-absorbing "gel" are often used to keep food fresh. This is the second-most abundant element in Earth's crust, behind oxygen. For 10 points, many semiconductors are made using what metalloid symbolized Si ("S-I")?

This piece's first movement opens with an Adagio melody that is first stated by the cellos, before a trumpet enters with two sforzando Es. The Scherzo 3rd movement of this piece was adapted from its composer's aborted opera The Song of Hiawatha, and borrows rhythms from the folk songs of his native Bohemia. This piece's Largo 2nd movement features a prominent solo for the cor anglais and its first movement quotes the spiritual Swing Low, Sweet Chariot. For 10 points, name this symphony by Antonin Dvořák, inspired by melodies heard in America.
acceptableAnswers: Dvorak’s 9th Symphony before mention of Dvorak’s name

parts.text: Perhaps C.P.E. Bach's most famous composition is this blistering keyboard piece in C minor. Almost fully monophonic, this piece can be performed with the left hand alone, although many students learn it with both hands.

C.P.E. Bach also composed an E-flat major concerto for the unusual combination of piano and this other instrument, which along with the piano and clavichord was one of the most common keyboard instruments in the 18th century. The strings inside this keyboard instrument are plucked instead of hammered.

J.S. Bach's Well-Tempered Clavier was meant to showcase the benefits of well-tempering as opposed to mean tempering on keyboard instruments. To illustrate those benefits, the Well-Tempered Clavier includes this many pairs of preludes and fugues, one for every major and minor key in Western classical music.

bonuses.leadin: J.S. Bach produced a large number of compositions and a large number of children. Answer some questions about one of his sons, Carl Philipp Emanuel Bach, for 10 points each.

parts.text: Name this American school of thought centralized in the Northeast, whose notable members included Henry David Thoreau.
The founder and main proponent of Transcendentalism was this poet and essayist of "Nature" and "Self-Reliance".

One of Thoreau's most notable works is Walden , which is about the two years he spent living in a cabin on this type of water feature. This kind of feature is usually smaller than a lake and is also popular for ice-skating in the winter.

bonuses.leadin: This literary movement's core ideas focused on the power of the individual and emphasized the importance of beauty and nature. For 10 points each:

parts.text: This author is known for controversial works, such as one in which Humbert Humbert, a middle aged man, becomes obsessed with the 12-year-old Dolores Haze; other works by him include Pale Fire.
He depicted the lives of the Russian homeless in his play The Lower Depths and a cholera outbreak in in Children of the Sun; his novels include My Childhood and My University.
He wrote a comedy in five acts titled A Month in the Country but is perhaps better known for his nihilism in Fathers and Sons.

bonuses.leadin: For 10 points each, identify these Russian authors.

parts.text: Name this author of a novel in which Murphy dreams about Belacqua. Malone Dies is part of a trilogy of novels he wrote while in Paris.

Samuel Beckett was intrigued by the lazy lute maker Belacqua who appears in this section of a larger poem. In this section, the protagonist makes his way up seven terraces of a mountain, the entrance to which is guarded by Cato the Younger.
This British writer created the character of Lyra Belacqua in his series His Dark Materials.

bonuses.leadin: In this author's collection More Pricks Than Kicks, Belacqua Shuah struggles with the prospect of killing a lobster. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name these groups whose order is n factorial over 2 for some degree n. The instance of these groups of degree 5 is the smallest non-solvable group.
Alternating groups contain only the "even" examples of these things, which are the elements of a symmetric group. Order does matter for these rearrangements of a set, unlike combinations.

This man is the alphabetically-first namesake of the theorem which states that polynomials of degree 5 or greater don't have general solutions, which is partially because A5 is the smallest unsolvable group. Groups named for this man have a commutative binary operation.

bonuses.leadin: These groups are always normal subgroups in the groups they are derived from, as they are index-2. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Identify this shape that can be graphed by the equation x2+y2=1 ("x squared plus y squared equals one") in Cartesian coordinates.
A tangent line to a circle at a point has this relationship with the radius to that point. Two lines with this relationship form a 90 degree angle.
If the slope of a line is -2 (negative two), what is the slope of a line perpendicular to it?

bonuses.leadin: This shape can be graphed by the function r=2 in polar coordinates. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this play, which sees Nora Helmer's life fall apart after she can't pay back her loan to Nils Krogstad.
Name this Norwegian playwright of A Doll's House, Hedda Gabler, and The Master Builder.
In this play, the title character travels around the world and meets the Button Moulder, but eventually comes back to Solveig. Edvard Grieg wrote incidental music to it.

bonuses.leadin: The protagonist tries to embolden Torvald, before literally slamming the door on their marriage. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name the primary structure associated with autoimmune diseases.
What is the main function of the vaccine in the immune system?
Name another component of the immune system related to autoimmune diseases.

bonuses.leadin: For 10 points each, answer these questions about the human immune system.

parts.text: Identify this short story in which the Loisels [lwa-ZELLs] work for ten years to pay off loans to conceal that they lost the titular piece of jewelry, which Madame Forestier [fore-est-ee-AY] later reveals was a fake.
This short-story writer of "Mademoiselle Fifi" and "Ball of Fat" is probably best known for writing "The Necklace."
This other French writer of Sodom and Gomorrah is best known for his seven volume work In Search of Lost Time.

bonuses.leadin: The Ministry of Education invites the main characters to a party, and then one of them cries because she hasn't got a stitch to wear. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name the primary structure associated with cranial nerves.
What is the main function of the cranial nerve in the nervous system?
Name another component of the nervous system related to cranial nerves.

bonuses.leadin: For 10 points each, answer these questions about the human nervous system.

parts.text: Name this play in which King Philip II appoints Pedro Crespo to the title position.
In this other play by the author of The Mayor of Zalamea, Curcio hunts down Eusebio for killing his son Lisardo only to recognize him because he is wearing the title object.

The Mayor of Zalamea and Devotion to the Cross were written by this Spanish Golden Age playwright, a rival of Lope de Vega. He may be best known for his play about the imprisoned Polish prince Segismundo, Life is a Dream.

bonuses.leadin: In this play, the egomaniacal Don Alvaro abducts and rapes Isabel, the daughter of the man billeting him in his house. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name these things. Paul Benacerraf's identification problem poses philosophical issues with treating these things as abstract sets, as in von Neumann's construction.
Field's project critiques a position in the philosophy of math that analogizes objects like numbers to this ancient Greek thinker's theory of forms, which he developed in dialogues like the Crito.
The "indispensability" argument for numbers was developed by Hilary Putnam and this Harvard philosopher of "Two Dogmas of Empiricism."

bonuses.leadin: Hartry Field's book "Science Without [these things]" builds up Newton's physics without them, showing they may not be "indispensable" for science. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this poet of Twenty Love Poems and a Song of Despair.
Pablo Neruda was a writer from this South American country, whose capital is Santiago.

Neruda's poetry was described as "[bringing] alive a continent's destiny and dreams" when he was given this prize in 1971. This specific prize was established in 1901 by the estate of a Swedish inventor.

bonuses.leadin: This poet wrote a collection that declares "tonight, I can write the saddest lines," and that ends with a poem that laments "in you, everything sank." For 10 points each,

parts.text: Name this fundamental constant in chemistry that represents the ratio of product characteristics to reactant characteristics at which the forward and reverse reactions proceed at the same rate.
This law governs the derivation of equilibrium constant expressions, including entering gases as partial pressures, dissolved species as concentrations, and solids and liquids as unity.
This principle says that a system in equilibrium that is subjected to a stress reacts in a way that counteracts the stress.

bonuses.leadin: Symbolized by a capital K, its value for the reverse of a reaction is the reciprocal of the value for the forward reaction. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this ancient civilization, which built settlements at La Venta and San Lorenzo, known for its sculptures of large stone heads.
The Olmecs were also the first to use this tree-derived substance, which gave them their name. This material was a key component in the ball of the Mesoamerican ballgame.
This civilization also played the aforementioned ballgame, using it to determine sacrifices to their god of war, Huitzilopochtli ["hwee-tsi-lo-pahcht-lee"].

bonuses.leadin: These people were some of the earliest known to populate the Yucatan Peninsula. For ten points each:

parts.text: Name this poetical form, examples of which make up the majority of the collection The Testament. One poem titled for this form ends "But where are the snows of yesteryear?" in Dante Gabriel Rossetti's translation.

These people title François Villon's ("fran-SWAH vee-YONʼs") ballade that contains the "yesteryear" refrain. Christine de Pizan, the author of the ballade "Alone am I," is best known for a "book" and a "treasure" about the "city of [these people]."
acceptableAnswers: accept The Book of the City of Ladies
Le Livre de la Cité des Dames
accept The Treasure of the City of Ladies
Le Trésor de la Cité des Dames

parts.text: This figure is the last mentioned in Villon's "Ballade of the Dead Ladies." Christine de Pizan's last work is a lyrical verse about this figure, but she died before this heroine was burnt at the stake in the Hundred Years' War.
acceptableAnswers: accept “The Tale of Joan of Arc”

bonuses.leadin: A poem in this form repeats the refrain "Alone am I and without a friend remain." For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name these businessmen such as Boris Berezovsky and Roman Abramovich who came to control many Russian industries following privatization during the 1990s.
The oligarchs gained their power during the presidency of this man, the first Russian president to be elected by a popular vote.

This oligarch who owned the oil company Yukos was imprisoned in 2003, likely because of his disagreements with Vladimir Putin more than for the charges of tax evasion and fraud. He was released in December 2013.

bonuses.leadin: Vladimir Potinin and Anatoly Chubais designed the "loans-for-shares" program that served these men. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this movement, named after a New York City neighborhood. African-American authors like Claude McKay and Langston Hughes were part of this movement.

Langston Hughes's poem "Harlem" opens by asking "What happens to a dream deferred? / Does it dry up / like [this specific item]?" Bruce Norris's play Clybourne Park was inspired by a play titled for this item.
In this poem, Hughes calls himself "the darker brother / They send me to eat in the kitchen" and later comments, "Tomorrow / I'll be at the table."

bonuses.leadin: A poem from this movement states "Although she feeds me bread of bitterness...I love this cultured hell that tests my youth." For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name these bonds that occur between polar molecules containing a certain element.
These intermolecular forces occur between non-polar molecules that have temporarily induced dipoles. They are a subset of van der Waals forces.

These noncovalent interactions in proteins are formed from a combination of hydrogen bonding and electrostatic interactions. They share their name with a device that connects the oxidation and reduction half-cells of a galvanic cell.

bonuses.leadin: These bonds explain why water has a high boiling point. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this cathedral, whose dome Nikolaus Pevsner dubbed "the most perfect in the world". The tomb of this building's architect is contained within and reads "reader, if you seek his monument - look around you".
St. Paul's is the mother church of this city, which is also the site of Temple Church and Westminster Abbey.
This lead architect of St. Paul's cathedral was commissioned to design fifty-two churches after the Fire of London in 1666.

bonuses.leadin: The dome of this building was inspired by the Romanesque lantern at Ely, where the architect's uncle was bishop. For 10 points each:
